title: Resolve secrets/browser_cookies.json from session dir, not CWD
description: main.rs:5255-5266 reads 'secrets/browser_cookies.json' relative to the process working directory. Running 'li' from any directory with that file (other repo, /tmp, attacker drop) silently swaps in those cookies. Resolve relative to Session::default_path().parent(), or require explicit --cookies-file flag. At minimum print absolute path in the eprintln so the user can verify identity. Security review M5 (2026-04-29).
close_reason: Landed in 71c7f09 / pushed as 34766ae. Resolution: session.rs gained browser_cookies_path() helper resolving to LINKEDIN_COOKIES_FILE env var or <session_dir>/browser_cookies.json; never CWD. eprintln prints absolute canonicalized path. Three unit tests.

title: Sanitize raw API response bodies in error messages
description: Every Error::Api { body } / Error::Auth carries the raw response payload (linkedin-api/src/error.rs:19-25, client.rs:441-449/2440-2469/2520-2529) and the CLI surfaces it via format!('API call failed: {e}'). LinkedIn 4xx/5xx bodies routinely include connection names, conversation snippets, member URNs. Define a SafeError variant that retains status + correlation ID and truncates body to ~200 chars with PII heuristics stripped. Mirrors the pattern graduated for the public360 MCP server. Security review H1 (2026-04-29).
notes:
Plan: don't change Error variant shape (40+ construction sites would migrate; is_retriable_graphql_error and other internal logic substring-match on raw body — can't sanitize at construction). Instead, sanitize at the Display boundary.

1. error.rs gains sanitize_body() helper that:
   - truncates to MAX_DISPLAY_BODY_LEN (200 chars at char boundary)
   - masks LinkedIn URNs (urn:li:<type>:<opaque-id> -> urn:li:<type>:[…])
   - masks email-shaped strings (local@domain -> [email])
   - appends ' …[N more]' suffix when truncated
2. impl Display by hand (replacing thiserror #[error] for Api/Auth variants); other variants keep #[error].
3. Tests cover the sanitization helper and the through-the-Display surface.

Correlation ID capture deferred — that's a separate enhancement (add x-li-uuid header capture to check_response, threaded into Error::Api). File a follow-up bead.
close_reason:
Display-boundary sanitization landed. error.rs gained:
- sanitize_body() helper: mask LinkedIn URNs to urn:li:<type>:[…], mask emails to [email], truncate to 200 bytes at UTF-8 char boundary with '…[N more bytes]' suffix
- ApiBodyDisplay/AuthDisplay wrapper types used in thiserror #[error("...")] templates so Error::Api and Error::Auth render sanitized while the raw body field remains accessible (is_retriable_graphql_error continues to substring-match on it)
- 9 new unit tests covering URN masking (single, multiple, partial), email masking, short-body preservation, truncation, char-boundary safety, and end-to-end Display for both variants

Why not change variant shape: 40+ Error::Api construction sites would migrate, and is_retriable_graphql_error substring-matches on the raw body. Sanitizing at the Display boundary touches one place and leaves all internal pattern matching intact.

Correlation-ID capture deferred to follow-up bead linkedin-rs-mk5.

title: Use typed CliError instead of String error type
description: The CLI returns Result<_, String> from every command (~132 map_err sites) and stringifies the well-typed linkedin_api::error::Error at the boundary. Define enum CliError { Api(linkedin_api::error::Error), Session(String), Cache(String), Input(String) } in linkedin-cli/src/error.rs. Refactor command sigs and replace classify_error/error_hint regex-on-strings with match arms on the enum. Architectural review item H1 (2026-04-29). Should land first since it unblocks downstream extraction work.
notes:
Plan (large cross-cutting refactor):

1. linkedin-cli/src/error.rs (new):
   - enum CliError { Api(linkedin_api::Error), Session(String), Cache(String), Input(String), Other(String) }
   - impl Display via thiserror (#[error] templates)
   - impl From<linkedin_api::Error> -> CliError::Api
   - impl From<serde_json::Error> -> CliError::Other (formatted)
   - type CliResult<T> = Result<T, CliError>
   - exit_code() method on CliError replacing substring-based classify_error
   - hint() method on CliError replacing substring-based error_hint (matches on Api inner Error::Api { status })

2. linkedin-cli/src/util.rs:
   - exit_on_err takes CliResult<()>
   - classify_error / error_hint substring versions deleted
   - util tests updated to construct CliError variants and assert on .hint() / .exit_code()

3. main.rs:
   - exit_on_err wired against CliResult<()>; no other dispatch logic changes

4. Each domain module (auth, profile, messages, feed/*, connections, search, company, events, notifications, session):
   - cmd_* sigs: Result<T, String> -> CliResult<T>
   - helper sigs (load_session, load_session_client, resolve_post_urn, etc): String -> CliError
   - map_err(|e| format!('...: {e}')) on linkedin_api::Error: replace with ? (From impl handles it)
   - map_err over serde_json::Error: replace with ? (From impl)
   - ad-hoc string errors (validation, cache parse): wrap as CliError::Input / Cache / Session

5. e2e gate: build, all tests pass (util tests will need rewrites), clippy, fmt
close_reason:
linkedin-cli/src/error.rs is the new home for the typed CliError enum: Api(linkedin_api::Error) via thiserror's #[from], plus Session/Cache/Input/Other(String) variants. CliResult<T> alias and an exit_code module live alongside.

exit_code() and hint() now match on the typed variant rather than substring-matching the formatted message. The 401-and-auth-and-session branch all route to exit_code::AUTH; 429/403/301/200-with-transient-graphql get their own hint arms; Input(msg) carrying 'out of range' routes to the cache-repopulation hint.

util.rs lost ~80 lines: classify_error/error_hint and their substring tables are gone. exit_on_err now takes CliResult<()> and calls e.exit_code() / e.hint(). The six string-shaped hint tests in util.rs moved into error.rs as typed-variant tests, plus four new ones covering exit_code routing and the 403 hint that the prior tests didn't reach.

Cross-cutting sweep across 18 CLI modules (auth, company, connections, events, messages, notifications, profile, search, every feed/* + session) via two Python regex passes plus 9 manual fixes for multi-line literals / helper fns returning String:
- Result<X, String> -> CliResult<X> (22 cmd_* sigs + ~12 helpers)
- .map_err(|e| format!('API call failed: {e}'))? -> ?  (From<linkedin_api::Error> handles it)
- .map_err(|e| format!('JSON format error: {e}'))? -> ?  (From<serde_json::Error> handles it)
- Err('...'.to_string()) -> Err(CliError::Input('...'.to_string())) for validation, ::Other for misc
- .ok_or_else(|| format!(...)) -> .ok_or_else(|| CliError::<variant>(format!(...)))
- thiserror 2 added as linkedin-cli dep

e2e gate clean: 120 tests pass (94 linkedin-api + 2 smoke + 24 cli, up from 19 because error.rs added 10 typed-error tests replacing the 6 stringy util tests), clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean.

Behavioral wins for users: scripts that 'if [ $? -eq 2 ]; then re-login' now actually catch CliError::Session and Api(Auth) — previously a session error from session.rs went through .to_string() and hit the AUTH pattern by accident. Hint text for 'index out of range' fires from CliError::Input regardless of the surrounding format string, where the old version only matched if the literal phrase made it through unaltered.

title: Bump GitHub Actions to Node.js 24-compatible versions
description: GitHub will force Node.js 24 by default on 02-06-2026 and remove Node.js 20 from runners on 16-09-2026. The CI annotation observed on run 25124977134 (29-04-2026) flagged actions/checkout@v4 as still running on Node.js 20. Audit .github/workflows/ for any actions still pinned to Node-20 versions (checkout, rust-cache, etc.), bump to current major versions that publish Node-24 builds. Re-run a CI job and confirm the deprecation annotation is gone. No code change expected outside .github/workflows/.

title: Add 'connections withdraw <invitation_urn>' (RE capture required)
description: Every invite the CLI sends is now an outstanding Pending; users have no way to undo via CLI. The withdraw flow likely lives on the same MemberRelationships resource under a different action. Capture the live web withdraw flow (Pending → click → confirm), document body shape in re/connection_request.md, then add the command. Uses the same retry middleware once it lands.
notes: Investigation 2026-04-29: re/invitations.md already documents the WITHDRAW action in InvitationActionsRepository. Sibling action 'accept' is implemented at linkedin/linkedin-api/src/client.rs:1902 (path: voyagerRelationshipsDashInvitations/{urn}?action=accept, body: {invitationUrn, sharedSecret}). Withdraw likely parallels — replace 'accept' with 'withdraw' in path. BUT: no get_sent_invitations() exists yet (only get_invitations() for received), so users can't easily obtain the URN. Bead's 'RE capture required' tag still stands — need to verify (a) WITHDRAW body shape matches, (b) sent-invitation URN format, (c) whether sent invitations have sharedSecret field. Captured live web flow would resolve all three.

title: Add custom-invite/preload page as fallback slug→URN resolver
description: When the GraphQL profile resolver returns transient downstream errors, hitting linkedin.com/preload/custom-invite/?vanityName=<slug> returns the resolved URN in the response (the modern web client uses this as a server-side resolver). Add it as a fallback after the GraphQL retry middleware exhausts its retries. More reliable than retry-and-pray when the GraphQL path is genuinely down.
notes: Added resolve_profile_urn_via_preload as a final fallback after the existing 3-step REST/GraphQL chain. Pulls /preload/custom-invite/?vanityName=<slug>, finds the publicIdentifier:<slug> marker in the embedded HTML-escaped JSON state, walks back ~500 bytes to grab the paired entityUrn. Disambiguates correctly from the viewer's own URN that also appears earlier in the page (me-menu/global nav). 4 unit tests including the disambiguation case and an out-of-window negative.

title: Expose mentions in 'notifications list' / add 'notifications mentions N'
description: Notifications carry an underlying post URN; the post body has structured mention data with fsd_profile URNs. Surface that list either inline (--with-mentions flag on list) or as a separate subcommand 'notifications mentions N' indexing into last list. Closes the workflow gap where users have to chase the post URL to enumerate who else was tagged.
notes: Investigation 2026-04-29: cmd_notifications_list at linkedin/linkedin-cli/src/main.rs:4842, get_notifications at client.rs:961. print_notification_card already extracts contentPrimaryText[0].text but treats it as flat string. No notifications cache exists — would need to add last_notifications.json paralleling feed_cache_path() at main.rs:5317. NO documentation in re/ for the structured mention shape (attributesV2 entries with MEMBER_MENTION type + fsd_profile URN). The post body fetch via permalink endpoint is also undocumented (overlaps with linkedin-rs-0hw). Two captures needed: (1) a notification card with mention metadata to confirm whether attributesV2 lives on contentPrimaryText[0] or fetched separately, (2) the permalink endpoint to fetch the underlying post body. Suggest implementing 0hw first since oau depends on its endpoint.

title: Add '--summary' flag to 'profile view' for compact output
description: Default --json dumps ~150KB per profile including positions, education, certifications, ring status, etc. Add --summary that returns only: full URN, public ID, name, headline, location, relationship state (connection/noConnection/etc), follower count. Plays well with batch flows and avoids hitting the output-size guard.
notes: Added --summary flag to profile view that returns compact JSON: name, public ID, full URN, headline, location, industry, relationshipState (the union key inside memberRelationship.memberRelationship), followerCount. New extract_profile_summary helper with 3 unit tests. Conflicts with --json (clap-enforced). Follower count is sourced from profileProfileActions.overflowActionsResolutionResults[].followingState.followerCount.

title: Classify CLI errors with actionable next-step hints
description: Today errors like 'API error (HTTP 301): {"status":301}' or 'failed to resolve profile' offer no diagnostic signal. Add a thin classifier that distinguishes: auth-stale (suggest 'li auth login'), endpoint-retired (suggest checking re/ docs and filing an issue), rate-limited (suggest backoff), transient (already retried by the new middleware). Output the hint as a second line on stderr.
notes: Added error_hint(msg) returning Some(&'static str) when an error matches a known shape: HTTP 401 (suggests li auth login), HTTP 301 (endpoint retired — check re/ docs), HTTP 429 (rate limited), GraphQL transient (retried already), failed to resolve profile (suggest URN or search invite N), HTTP 403 (captcha), index out of range (rerun parent command). 6 unit tests. Hint prints as a second line on stderr after the error message; exit code is unchanged.

title: Make 'feed view <urn>' fall back to the post permalink endpoint
description: Currently 'feed view' only works if the post is in the last 50 scanned feed items, returning a 404 otherwise. Add a fallback path that fetches the post via LinkedIn's permalink endpoint (the same one /feed/update/<urn> hits in the web UI) so any activity URN works. Keep the cache-hit fast path.
notes: Investigation 2026-04-29: get_post() at linkedin/linkedin-api/src/client.rs:516 currently fetches feed/updates?q=findFeed&start=0&count=50 and scans for activity ID match. cmd_feed_view at linkedin/linkedin-cli/src/main.rs:5597 calls it directly. Permalink endpoint NOT documented in re/. api_endpoint_catalog.md shows feed/updates/{updateId}?action=feedback (POST actions only) — GET-by-URN permalink path/params unknown. Need to capture web flow: visit linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:N in browser devtools, log the voyager API call. Likely candidates to verify: feed/updates/{urlEncodedUrn}, feed/feedDashUpdatesV2/{urn}, or a Dash GraphQL finder. Once endpoint known, fallback should: 1) try cache scan (current 50-item path), 2) on miss, hit permalink endpoint, 3) only error if both miss.

title: Add 'search invite N' that uses last search-people result by index
description: Mirror the 'feed read N' / 'feed comments N' pattern: after a search people query, allow inviting the Nth result by its row index in the printed list. Removes the URN-extraction friction users hit when piping search results into invite. Reuse the existing search cache file.
notes: Added 'search invite <index>' subcommand. Pulls fsd_profile URN out of cached entityResult (preferred path — bypasses GraphQL profile resolver entirely) and falls back to slug if entityUrn/trackingUrn are absent. New SearchPersonTarget struct + resolve_search_person_target helper. 3 unit tests cover URN-preferred, slug-fallback, and label formatting.

title: Add 'connections invite-batch' for newline-separated URNs/slugs
description: Replace the bash-loop pattern users currently rely on. Read URNs/slugs from --from-file or stdin, send each through send_connection_request with built-in 2s pacing and per-line success/failure reporting. Should depend on the new retry middleware so transient failures don't break a 50-item batch.
notes: Added 'connections invite-batch --from-file <path|->' that reads slugs/URNs (one per line, # comments and blanks ignored) and sends each with pacing_ms delay (default 2s). Tab-separated stdout: <input>\tOK\t<invitation_urn> or <input>\tFAIL\t<reason>. Continues through failures unless --stop-on-error is set; closes with a summary line on stderr. Uses the new GraphQL retry middleware so transient downstream errors don't break a 50-line batch. 2 unit tests on the parser (parse_batch_targets).

title: Retry transient GraphQL 'Internal error fetching data from downstream' errors
description: LinkedIn's GraphQL mesh returns transient downstream errors at HTTP 200 with a body that mixes partial data and error strings. Today the client treats them as terminal, leaking out as hard CLI errors. Add bounded exponential backoff (max 2 retries; 500ms then 1500ms) inside the post/get layer for this specific error class. Don't retry on auth errors or 4xx-equivalent shapes. Test with a fault-injecting fake transport.
notes: Wrapped graphql_get and graphql_post in retry loops keyed off is_retriable_graphql_error, which matches HTTP-200 GraphQL bodies containing 'Internal error fetching data from downstream' or 'Failed to get response from server'. Reuses existing MAX_RETRIES / BASE_BACKOFF_MS / MAX_BACKOFF_MS constants. 6 new unit tests.

title: Migrate send_connection_request from retired normInvitations to Dash endpoint
description: LinkedIn retired the legacy voyagerGrowthNormInvitations endpoint. As of 29-04-2026 every POST returns HTTP 301. Fix: switch to voyagerRelationshipsDashInvitations?action=create. Body schema captured from live web UI since the Dash schema in the RE doc was incomplete.
notes: Captured the modern endpoint from a live web Connect flow. The replacement is voyagerRelationshipsDashMemberRelationships?action=verifyQuotaAndCreateV2&decorationId=...InvitationCreationResultWithInvitee-2 — neither the legacy normInvitations nor the Dash Invitations route the RE doc anticipated. Body is just {invitee:{inviteeUnion:{memberProfile:<full-urn>}}}; no trackingId. Smoke-tested on one URN with the new code; LinkedIn returned a fresh fsd_invitation URN. Follow-ups (out of scope): with-note message placement is unverified, email invitee variant unmapped, withdraw flow likely also moved to MemberRelationships.

title: events attendees returns empty on stale session
description: First call to li events attendees returned empty elements array. Same call worked after Chrome browsed LinkedIn (likely refreshed shared cookies). Investigate: should CLI detect stale sessions and prompt re-auth? Should it warn instead of silently returning empty?
close_reason: Already resolved by 2a0bad8 (Add events commands: view details and list attendees). cmd_event_attendees in linkedin/linkedin-cli/src/main.rs:6052-6062 detects the empty-on-stale-session case via a get_event probe and prints a warning to stderr telling the user to refresh cookies and re-run `li auth login`. Bead never got closed when the fix landed; cleaning up retroactively.

title: Deduplicate main.rs dispatch_events / dispatch_company / dispatch_notifications
description:
Codescene flagged main.rs for duplication between dispatch_events and dispatch_company (and pattern repeats with dispatch_notifications). The three dispatchers are 10-line near-clones since the client.rs per-resource split: each takes a *Action enum, matches on the variants, and threads to a cmd_* function.

Options: macro_rules! dispatch_action that takes the enum + variant->fn mapping; or push the action into a trait that each domain implements. Macro is simpler and more discoverable.

Source: /tmp/linkedin-rs-audit/codescene-cli.md (Carlini audit 17-05-2026).

title: Thread newtype URN types through linkedin-api to clear String-Heavy Function Arguments
description:
Codescene flags 'String-Heavy Function Arguments' across client.rs, client/feed.rs (46%), client/messaging.rs (53%), and others. LinkedIn URN strings are the dominant offender — every method takes raw String where a typed Urn / PostUrn / ConversationUrn / ProfileUrn would work.

The newtype machinery already exists or can live in linkedin-api/src/urn.rs (the module that just got created during 5jw). Wrap LinkedIn URN strings as transparent newtypes, add From<&str> / Display impls, then sweep the per-resource client methods to take the newtype.

Expected blast radius: linkedin-api per-resource client modules + a one-shot CLI sweep where callers construct the newtype at the boundary. Internal codescene scores for the affected files should jump from 9.5-9.7 to 10.0 after the change.

Source: /tmp/linkedin-rs-audit/codescene-api.md (Carlini audit 17-05-2026).

title: Split linkedin-api/src/models.rs (1242 LoC, fan-in 11)
description:
models.rs is the largest single file in the workspace at 1242 LoC, and Ridge's arch_boundaries scan flagged it as the highest-fan-in module (11 importers spanning both crates). Mirror the per-resource split that already exists for the client/ submodule — feed_models.rs, profile_models.rs, messaging_models.rs, connections_models.rs, search_models.rs, etc.

Source: /tmp/linkedin-rs-audit/ridge-arch.md (Carlini audit 17-05-2026).

title: Refactor print_wvmp_viewer_card (Bumpy Road + cc=10)
description:
profile.rs::print_wvmp_viewer_card (L553-600) is the only function in linkedin-cli double-flagged by Codescene: Bumpy Road (bumps=2) AND Complex Method (cc=10). It walks five WVMP card variants in sequence with early returns and is the most concrete refactor target in the crate.

Source: /tmp/linkedin-rs-audit/codescene-cli.md (Carlini audit 17-05-2026).

Suggested approach: extract a small renderer per variant (render_profile_view, render_private_viewer, render_generic, render_anon, render_premium_upsell), keep print_wvmp_viewer_card as a dispatch table. The WVMP_* constants are already imported from linkedin_api::restli, so the per-variant fns can be tight.

title: extract_activity_urn doesn't trim trailing ',MEMBER_SHARES' suffix
description:
linkedin-api/src/urn.rs::extract_activity_urn() reads until ')' but not until ','. For a feed entityUrn like 'urn:li:fs_updateV2:(urn:li:activity:7312345,MEMBER_SHARES,DEFAULT,…)' the returned value is 'urn:li:activity:7312345,MEMBER_SHARES,…' rather than 'urn:li:activity:7312345'.

Discovered while moving the function from feed/urn.rs to linkedin-api/src/urn.rs (bead 5jw). Out of scope for the move — preserved existing behavior.

Investigate which callers (search.rs:254, 259, 269; feed/my_posts.rs:56) tolerate the suffix vs which break. If any break, change the end-finder to stop on the first non-(alnum:_-.) character, not specifically ')'.

If everything tolerates it (because LinkedIn endpoints are lax), keep as-is and document the lax behavior with a test like extract_activity_urn_stops_at_paren.
notes:
Confirmed via caller analysis: feed/my_posts.rs:55 carries a literal workaround — '.split(\',\').next().unwrap_or(&u).to_string()' — applied to the result of extract_activity_urn() to trim the suffix this bead is about. That's the proof. Fix the parser, remove the workaround.

Fix: tighten the end-finder. Currently 'rest.find(\')\')', new: 'rest.find(|c| !(c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == \':\' || c == \'-\' || c == \'_\' || c == \'.\'))' — same predicate as the sibling extract_activity_urn_from_url. Stop at any char that can't appear in a URN.
close_reason:
Tightened end-of-URN detection. extract_activity_urn now stops on the first non-URN character (anything outside alnum/:/-/_/.), not just on ')'. Replaces the older 'stop at )' behavior and the workaround in feed/my_posts.rs:55 that was doing .split(',').next() inline.

Two new tests: extract_activity_urn_strips_member_shares_suffix covers the actual Voyager shape 'urn:li:fs_updateV2:(urn:li:activity:NNN,MEMBER_SHARES,DEFAULT,false)' → 'urn:li:activity:NNN'; extract_activity_urn_stops_at_whitespace covers prose-embedded URNs. The existing extract_activity_urn_stops_at_paren keeps passing.

Removed the inline workaround at feed/my_posts.rs:55 — activity_urn no longer needs the .split(',').next() pass.

e2e gate clean: 96 + 2 + 24 + 0 = 122 tests pass (+2 new), clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean.

title: Capture LinkedIn correlation ID in Error::Api / Error::Auth
description:
Follow-up to 6cs: the sanitization fix landed but the bead originally asked for status + correlation ID. We retain status; correlation ID is still missing.

LinkedIn responses carry a per-request correlation header (x-li-uuid and/or x-li-tracker on Voyager + Dash endpoints). Wire it through check_response (and the GraphQL post path in client.rs) into a new Option<String> field on Error::Api, surfaced via Display. With the ID, support reports against LinkedIn rate-limits / 5xx storms become traceable to the specific server-side request without exposing PII.

Scope:
- check_response: read x-li-uuid (or fall back to x-li-tracker) from response headers
- Extend Error::Api with correlation_id: Option<String>
- Same for the GraphQL 200-with-errors path in client.rs
- Display becomes 'API error (HTTP {status}, request_id={id}): {sanitized body}' when ID is present
notes:
Plan:

1. Add 'correlation_id: Option<String>' field to Error::Api in linkedin-api/src/error.rs
2. Update Display impl: 'API error (HTTP {status}{maybe ', request_id={id}'}): {sanitized body}'
3. Update internal::check_response to extract from response headers BEFORE consuming the body. LinkedIn's correlation header isn't documented in re/, so the extractor walks a candidate list (x-li-uuid, x-li-tracker-uuid, x-li-fabric, x-li-tracking-id) and takes the first present.
4. Update GraphQL post path in client.rs (~460) to do the same.
5. Update all 22 Error::Api construction sites to pass correlation_id (None for validation/format errors, extracted value for response-shaped errors)
6. Update match patterns (is_retriable_graphql_error, error.rs tests) to use '..' to ignore the new field
7. New test: Display includes 'request_id=' when correlation is Some
8. New test: extract_correlation_id picks from candidate list
close_reason:
Error::Api now carries a correlation_id: Option<String> field. The Display impl renders 'API error (HTTP {status}, request_id={id}): {body}' when present, falling back to 'API error (HTTP {status}): {body}' otherwise — no surprises for existing error consumers.

Header extraction (extract_correlation_id) walks a candidate list (x-li-uuid, x-li-tracker-uuid, x-li-tracking-id, x-li-fabric) and returns the first non-empty value. Order is the order LinkedIn most likely uses; the list is in linkedin-api/src/error.rs and is one line to extend.

Three HTTP-response paths now pass the extracted ID through to Error::Api: client/internal.rs::check_response, client.rs::check_response_retryable, client.rs::decode_graphql_post_error. The same paths' 401-paths fold 'request_id=…' into the Auth error message via a suffix variable.

22 Error::Api construction sites in linkedin-api updated (mechanical sweep via Python regex with manual fixes for two match-pattern shapes that needed '..' instead of 'correlation_id: None'). is_retriable_graphql_error and the test-helper api_err(...) in linkedin-cli got the same '..' treatment.

5 new tests in linkedin-api: extract_correlation_id_returns_first_match, ..._falls_back_through_candidates, ..._returns_none_when_absent, ..._skips_empty_values, display_for_api_includes_request_id_when_present. Existing display test now also asserts the absence of 'request_id' when correlation is None.

e2e gate clean: 127 tests pass (101 + 2 + 24, +6 net new), clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean.

title: Split main.rs into per-domain modules
description: main.rs is 7,198 LOC. Natural seams: feed.rs (~750 LOC), profile.rs (~860), connections.rs (~430), search.rs (~240), notifications.rs (~315), messages.rs (~350), company.rs (~290), events.rs, auth.rs, cache.rs, format.rs. Each owns its cmd_* functions plus its private print_* formatters. main.rs keeps Cli/Commands/main()/dispatch — should fall under 400 LOC. Architectural review M1 (2026-04-29). Do AFTER H1/H2/H3 land so the moved code already uses the typed error and shared helpers — otherwise the cleanup gets duplicated.
notes: Split landed. main.rs is now 323 LOC (was 7,198). All 14 per-domain modules from the bead exist: auth, cli, company, connections, events, feed/ (module dir), graphql_print, messages, notifications, profile, search, session, spam, util. Shipped across commits 8c6fb57 (feed/), 5838249 (profile), 519e4c0 (messages), 277b247 (connections), e4cfd43 (search), d767d0d (company), d437ae8 (linkedin-api client split), plus the per-file Code Health work that followed. The bead's blocking-order warning (do AFTER H1/H2/H3 land) did NOT hold: split shipped first. Blockers linkedin-rs-0c5 (typed CliError), -5jw (move parsers to linkedin-api), -78s (move union helpers) remain open. Re-touching the per-domain modules when those land is real future cost; track that work under those beads, not here.

title: Tune Cargo release profile and prune tokio features
description: No [profile.release] block in linkedin/Cargo.toml. Add lto='thin', codegen-units=1, strip='symbols' — drops 'li' binary from ~12MB to ~5MB. Also: tokio uses features=['full'] but only needs ['macros','rt-multi-thread','process','signal','time']; full pulls in fs/net/io-util/parking_lot adding ~15-20s compile penalty + 300KB. Consider switching #[tokio::main] to flavor='current_thread' (saves ~5ms cold start). Performance review M4+M5 (2026-04-29).
close_reason: Landed in a298ebb / pushed as 1f33c02. Resolution: workspace Cargo.toml gained [profile.release] (lto='thin', codegen-units=1, strip='symbols'). linkedin-cli tokio features pruned from ['full'] to ['macros','rt-multi-thread','time']. Release binary measured 6.2MB. Kept rt-multi-thread for cmd_inbox's parallel reqwest calls.

title: Validate cookie names in with_browser_cookies
description: linkedin-api/src/client.rs:151-164 concatenates HashMap-keyed cookie names into Cookie header strings without validation. A malformed name with control chars / extra attributes could (in principle) inject Set-Cookie headers if the file source is ever less trusted. Reqwest rejects most malformed cookies today so this is posture-weakening, not exploitable. Validate names against [A-Za-z0-9_-]+ before append, or use reqwest::cookie::Cookie::build. Security review M6 (2026-04-29).
close_reason: Landed in c48c8f0 / pushed as a3e7f5e. Resolution: linkedin-api/src/client.rs gained is_valid_cookie_name() helper validating against [A-Za-z0-9_-]+. with_browser_cookies silently skips entries with invalid names. Two unit tests covering real LinkedIn cookie names and injection attempts.
